heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles flexible NinjaTek NinjaFlex 85A out of the box using its direct drive extruder, provided the volumetric flow is restricted to 2.8 mm³/s for a safe max print speed of 33 mm/s. No hardware upgrades are required, but filament must be fed directly via the rear spool holder rather than the AMS.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Glue Stick release agent (mandatory to prevent permanent bed bonding)
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 2.8 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent extruder jamming and filament bucking.
Bypass the AMS completely; configure the rear spool holder or external drybox feed path.
Lower Retraction Length to 0.8 mm and Retraction Speed to 25 mm/s to reduce the risk of soft filament wrapping around drive gears.
Disable 'Reduce infill retraction' and enable 'Avoid crossing walls' to minimize stringing and surface scarring on flexible perimeters.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Filament wrapping around the extruder gears or jamming before the hotend
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Volumetric flow rate or print speed is too high, causing backpressure that buckles the soft 85A filament inside the extruder.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Enforce a Maximum Volumetric Speed cap of 2.8 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer and keep max printing speeds below 33 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Excessive fine stringing, oozing, and branch-like whiskers
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption due to highly hygroscopic TPU chemistry combined with excessive travel moves.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament at 50°C-55°C for at least 8 hours prior to printing, and enable 'Avoid crossing walls' with a max detour distance in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PEI coating tearing off or parts permanently fused to the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Extremely high chemical adhesion between molten TPU and PEI surfaces upon cooling.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVA glue stick or liquid bed adhesive to act as a sacrificial release agent before starting the print.

faq.question: Can I feed NinjaTek NinjaFlex 85A through the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: No, flexible filaments softer than 95A will buckle and jam in the internal AMS drive funnels and long PTFE tubing; feed directly from the external spool holder.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped at only 33 mm/s on a high-speed printer like the X1C?
faq.answer: The highly compliant 85A shore hardness cannot support high extrusion pressures without buckling in the extruder gears, limiting volumetric throughput to 2.8 mm³/s.

faq.question: Should the Bambu Lab X1C chamber door be open or closed when printing NinjaFlex 85A?
faq.answer: Keep the top glass vented or front door propped slightly open if ambient temperature exceeds 25°C to avoid heat creep inside the direct drive assembly.

faq.question: Is a glue stick really necessary on a textured PEI plate for TPU?
faq.answer: Yes, TPU bonds aggressively to PEI surfaces; the glue stick functions as a vital separation release agent to prevent permanently damaging the build plate surface.
